chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Rhythm Town versus Jump, Jive & Jam
summary: Spikes explains that his operetta was titled Rhythm Town with Jump, Jive and Jam as a style tag and three comic characters.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Mmmmm hmmm. And then, the other show that I don't believe we've talked about at all was one that you did called "Jump, Jive & Jam."
Well, that's "Rhythm Town." They're both the same.
Uh, well, which was the title? Did it have two titles--a title and a subtitle?

I said, "Operetta of Jump, Jive & Jam," That means that that's the style--Jump, Jive & Jam. Now, I had characters in there named Jump, Jive and Jam--three comics, you see--but the name of the show was "Rhythm Town."

An operetta of Jump, Jive & Jam. Just like I'd say that so-and-so is the Home of the Blues...or the Home of the Disco. You see? This was "Jump, Jive & Jam." That's what the music they were playin' then, you know. Ever'body was jumpin' or jivin' and jammin'.
The reason I thought it was...
Yeah, because in this copy of The Sentinel, Thursday, January 17, 1946, it says, "McCoy will direct the 17-piece orchestra with 'Jump, Jive & Jam,'" And...
Well, that's what we started to call it--"Jump, Jive & Jam."
But by the time it opened, it was called "Rhythm Town."
